title: [Performance][Triton] Reuse MiniMax QK norm weights across tokens
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The fused MiniMax-M3 QK norm/RoPE/cache kernel prepares normalization weights for every token. Bound the logical grid by the device's vector-core count and process tokens cyclically within each program, so four weights and their Gemma scales can be reused across token iterations.

The implementation keeps one execution path and one launch. FP32 normalization, the BF16 rounding before RoPE, the extra main-K rounding, independent cache slots/strides, and query generation for padded tokens are preserved. Both request-dependent bounds remain runtime `do_not_specialize` arguments.

Tests add device-derived core boundaries and extend the request-size compilation sweep. The nightly reference now imports the scale-based helper and changes only `NUM_SLOTS` specialization, preserving runtime `NUM_TOKENS`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: lower fused-operator latency for prefill workloads on Ascend A3. Small workloads can regress; this implementation deliberately retains a single path rather than adding batch-specific dispatch. The public operator API is unchanged.

Matched whole-operator NPUGraph/NPU Event medians, in microseconds:

| Workload | Baseline | This change | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP4 verification, T=128 | 12.4501 | 11.9480 | 4.03% |
| TP4 verification, T=512 | 32.4202 | 29.8627 | 7.89% |
| TP8 prefill, T=8192 | 373.4926 | 332.8083 | 10.89% |
| TP4 prefill, T=32768 | 1894.9739 | 1782.7673 | 5.92% |

Small workloads were also repeated independently; both observations are retained:

| Workload | Main run baseline/change | Independent repeat baseline/change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TP8 T=1 | 3.6971 / 3.6501 | 3.3633 / 3.5604 |
| TP4 T=32 | 6.7375 / 7.0524 | 6.8717 / 6.6585 |
| TP4 T=40 | 7.5184 / 7.6656 | 7.8550 / 7.6289 |

These results do not establish an improvement for every batch size or a serving throughput improvement. The main run also had small regressions around the vector-core boundary, up to 2.86% in those boundary cases.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ascend A3 `Ascend910_9362`: 20 AI / 40 vector cores; CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, Triton 3.2.0.
- The complete updated operator and nightly test files ran through a standalone import shim in the A3 container: **95 passed, 6 skipped**. The skips are FP8 cases requiring A5. Production operator and test-file hashes were checked before and after execution. No full vLLM serving run was performed.
- Additional A3 compilation audit on torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, Triton 3.6.0 and bishengir 2.0.0: the two unchanged request/layout tests passed. Thirty request points plus warmup retain one JIT variant and one `_do_compile` entry; nine layout first visits create nine variants/entries, and nine revisits add zero. Source/test hashes remained unchanged. These are runtime compilation-entry counts, not disk-cache counts or a claim about all model graph buckets.
- Actual JIT dispatch/compile counters: 30 T/A/capacity sweeps retain one variant and one compilation entry; nine layouts compile once and revisiting them adds no compilation entries. The functional tests include core boundaries, full/partial RoPE, negative slots, cache preservation, separate inputs, empty input, and graph replay with changed positions/slots and concurrent memory traffic.
- A separate baseline/change comparison passed 38 cases. Every query and written cache row was checked in nonempty cases against the CPU reference; untouched cache regions were sampled. BF16 tolerances are `atol=0.032, rtol=0.01`; V copies are exact.
- Benchmark inputs are serving-shaped synthetic CP=1 workloads with BF16 activations/caches, D=128, rotary_dim=64, eps=1e-6, block_size=128, and 5392 main/index blocks. Local Q/KV/index-Q heads are `(8,1,1)` for TP8 packed projections and `(16,1,1)` for TP4 separate projections. Baseline is upstream commit `2880d19f8605baf59cc4d004ae4a5f0c5a3d1386`.
- Timing excludes compilation and Python allocation/submission: five warmups, 20 captured calls, ten replays per sample, five alternating-order samples. The independent small-workload repeat used 11 samples; it did not replace the main results.
- `msprof op` identifies both baseline and changed target kernels as AIV/vector, with 40 physical blocks. The baseline already used 40 physical blocks; the performance claim is not based on reducing physical block count.
- Applicable file-scoped Ruff, format, codespell, typos and Markdown checks passed. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but stopped while downloading the actionlint environment with an SSL EOF error. Full formatting/CI is not reported as passed.

Repository test targets, for an environment with vLLM-Ascend dependencies installed:

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_minimax_qknorm_rope_cache.py \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/test_minimax_qknorm_rope_cache_performance.py
```

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Device-derived core boundaries, empty inputs, padding, negative slots, cache strides and dynamic request sizes are covered.
- [ ] **Regression test**: Not applicable: this PR is a performance optimization and claims no correctness bug fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: Not applicable: no new error-handling path is introduced; existing API assertions are preserved.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Numerical/cache behavior and actual JIT counters are asserted.
- [x] **Performance impact**: Matched hardware results and small-workload regressions are included; nightly coverage is updated.

### PR submission checklist

- [x] The title contains the accepted `[Performance]` change-type tag.
- [x] Applicable test coverage, hardware configuration and validation results are recorded above.
- [ ] Required CI checks pass before merge. Pre-commit and CPU UT have passed for this head; selected A2/A3 E2E checks are still running in [the current CI run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41015914300).
- [ ] Outstanding NPU hardware or performance validation is completed before merge. Expanded operator measurements and MiniMax-M3 GPQA/GSM8K validation are in progress; FP8/A5 validation remains outstanding.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
